[b]The streets of the capital: Gossen:  March 7th, 2025[/b]

Word of the vote in the Chamber of the Peoples had filtered slowly through the grapevine of the media, dripping like a slow leak into the cup of the peoples. Now urgent voices whispered angrily in the streets as the city came awake with the rising sun of the 7th of March. 

It was to this that Alexander Mekedii strolled out from his domus. He had slept very little that night, the threat Theodora had made the day prior weighed greatly on his mind. Walking down the street he paused to see a man dressed in rags shouting something.

The tyrants! The tyrants! Behold the days have come when the veneer of justice has been torn! Cried the haggard old man, Alexander saw this and nodded briefly in agreement before continuing on.

Alexander had much to do that day, besides his official duties, he had to meet with one Sokola Porgyros, a silent leader of the nation's largest anti-dynastic protest groups, and a shadowy figure despite her relation to one of the dynastic families of the nation.

Sokola didnt like public exposure, and this went for her relations, as a result Alexander had to make a trek outside the ancient walls of the city of Gossen to a small out of the way rest stop, whose stone walls were painted in a layer of northern dust, and whose thatch and wood roof sagged dangerously inwards. 

Alexander entered the small structure, whose interior was not much better than the exterior, dirty plaster hung from the walls by what seemed like thread, and the bar that stood in the place stood crooked, the chairs looking as if they were to fall down at a single touch.

Looking around he caught the eye of a finely framed woman, her dark hair and eyes piercing through the shadowy space, smiling slightly as he walked towards the woman, bowing slightly he spoke, Greetings lady Porgyros, he began.

Spare me the civility, I know your tongue is much fiercer than that, replied Sokola

Ah yes my apologies, I forgot how you hate such things, replied Alexander sliding into the booth.

Now, tell me what you want, enquired Sokola.

The president plans on making a speech in a few days, in the Basilica, we want to pressure the guards into violence, stir up further unrest, prove the teeth of the government to the people, replied Alexander, sitting up slightly as Sokola stared him down.

I see, she replied, Then what next? she enquired.

Well we can use the violence as leverage against the president, force a recall, replied Alexander.

Sokola sighed, I will be willing to do this, however, I have contacts that have informed me the president might switch to a televised address, then what? she enquired.

Alexander frowned, he had not considered the fact that the president might move to a televised address, he thought the president too proud for such a thing, W-well, stuttered Alexander as he tried to come up with a counter, Well we could he continued causing Sokola to delve into a deep sigh.

I see, so you waste my time with your childish fantasies of revolt, forgetting that we live in a time where the government is more than capable at adapting to whatever threat might occur, sighed Sokola, clearly frustrated at his lack of thought into the manner, Heres what we are going to do, we are going to arrange a protest no matter what, in the meantime, if the president goes the televised route, I want you to begin pulling strings in the senate, you have allies right? she stated.

Alexander nodded, A few, he stated, his mind suddenly remembering the offer Theodora had made him. 

Good, use those then to continue stirring the waters, replied Sokola, We must move slowly, especially in this environment, she continued, anything else? she asked, inclining her head towards Alexander.

Nothing, replied Alexander resolutely.

Good, then you may go, she replied as Alexander rose, bowed to her once again, and then left the building, his mind rushing with ideas, perhaps he would compromise with Theodora, perhaps he might just accept the deal, but at what cost?

[b]MROS Dynamics and Brigrada XXIV[/b]

Delighted by the approval of the multi-million dollar contract, MROS Dynamics would swiftly begin setting up transportation routes to expedite the opening of a new operations facility in the ARoS. David Cyriacus, an ex-CAUSE special forces operator, would be assigned by MROS to take charge of corporate operations in Sikirsk, bringing SummitONE Solutions's overall international footprint to now four nations, five if counting Seagate Zurekdal as its own sovereign state.

MROS-branded private security guards would be swiftly stationed across all ARoS government palaces to serve as bodyguards and paramilitary escorts to the nation's key leaders, while in ARoS's military facilities the company would attempt to swiftly scrutinize Sikiriskian training methods to better drill the ARoS's dwindling supply of able-bodied soldiers. For now though, 3,000 men would be covertly brought in from High Albany to supplement the ARoS's forces.

Lastly, as a desperate bid to inject some much needed manpower beyond ARoS's regular armed forces, David Cyriacus would begin the process of organizing his own private militia out of Sikirsk's impoverished population, offering lucrative contracts to any native Sikirskians willing and able to join MROS Dynamics as temporary "security personnel", with various Sikirskian criminal syndicates, businessmen, and local warlords being invited to serve as commanders with promises of heavy funding and pensions after at least one year's worth of service.

While recruitment efforts would not bear fruit at the moment, MROS Dynamics would officially end their first day with a shortlist of around 1,000 Sikirskian conscripts and 4 new commanders into what would be formally referred to as the [i]Brigrada XXIV[/i] ("Brigade 24"). While nominally operating under the ARoS's regular armed forces, the Brigade would in fact be effectively independent and completely controlled by MROS Dynamics as an independent mercenary command. For this reason, the formation would become colloquially known in corporate parlance as the "Cyriacus Army" after its commander.

With the Armed Republic currently on the backfoot, MROS Dynamics and Brigrada XXIV would attempt some small-scale counteroffensives into Red Army and SLF territory, with Brigrada XXIV in particular being ordered east to face the SLF salient threatening the ARoS capital. MROS Dynamic mercenaries, meanwhile, would be stationed along the frontlines to check the advance of communist forces, hoping to stall for time until the arrival of fresh ARoS reinforcements.

[b]Measuring in Chimor [/b]- weight units
[b]Lukutíkrì[/b]: a measuring unit, it uses seeds of Lukumá as it base, is equivalent of 12 grams, and they are used as main type when measuring spices.
Example I: Chimor bought 6 Lukutíkrì of sugar, means, Chimor bought 72 grams of sugar.
Example II: this receipt need half a Lukutíkrì (6g)
[b]Chûño[/b]: not just a dried potato, the Chûño was used by farmers to weight fruits and vegetables, is equivalent of 50 grams.
Example I:a strawberry weights half a Chûño(27g, approximation).
Example II: this month, Chimor produced 360 chûños of apples (¡18kg of apples!).
[b]Pókuchês[/b]: each pókuchê is equal to 90 Chûños, or 4,5KG, is similar in function to the Chûño, as it is also used to measure weight of agriculture products.
Example: this harvest of kinoa was 10 Pókuches heavy(45kg).
Pókuches also, are ceramic pots for putting grains or fruits in it, full of Quinoa or corn, they can have up to 4,5kg.
[b] Mátmâ [/b]: how much a Mítmà worker can carry on average, is equal to 30KG, and is usually used for construction and other situations, but on general, construction is way more used.
Example; this stone  need 33 Mátmâs do be pulled, a stone measuring 1t, of course not too precise but do not expect much.
[b]Cól[/b]:how much a llama can carrying without exhausting, can be up to 50kg, loads carried by llamas were cases it would be used during long travels over the roads and routes.
Example : The caravan had with it 2 Cól of cocoa(100kg of cocoa).
[b]Tàmrak[/b]: meaning lost in time, is equal to 20 Cóls, or 1t, is commonly used for buildings and urban planning.
Example: the Chillakóri temple needed over 500 Tàmraks to be build(500t)

--------------------------------------
Other terms.
[b] Kánchâk [/b]: the Kánchâk is used in traditional myths, in some passages such as:
[i] Apû-Sáman hold a Kánchâk of mountains [/i].
The Kánchâk stands for a enormous imensurable mythological weight.

[b]Burán[/b]:this is used in Chimor bibles, early bibles and sometimes modern to refer the "weight Chísus Kráistú(Jesus Christ) carried", the only difference between this and the Kánchâk is , the Burán is used in christian cases, while the Kánchâk is used in traditional Chomuña waka religion.

[b]Interrogation[/b]

The five Sal-Baliz prisoners were woken at exactly 4:30am. They were served a small bowl of porridge each, and given fresh clothes (an orange prison uniform, nothing fancy). Once they had finished their bleak meal, the guards brought the first one into the interrogation chamber. 

The room was dimly lit, with only one light source. A bright lamp in the centre of the room, shining straight onto a chair. The chair had straps on it, designed to keep arms and legs still. At the back of the room an ominous figure stood waiting, General Eshaq Toraman, or Cobra-O1. As his Codename suggests, he is a member of cobra team (The armys anti-terrorist specialist unit). In fact, he is their highest ranking officer. Today he was playing the role of chief interrogator. The guards dragged the first prisoner forwards and strapped him into the chair. The prisoner was a male, around 20 years of age. He was the youngest of the five. Name, barked Eshaq sternly. The prisoner looked up at him with fear. What is your name? Inquired the general once again.
Karim Ahmadi, mumbled the prisoner after a brief moment of silence. A scribe was sat in the corner of the room, taking notes.
Now then Karim, we need to know some information you have and I can assure you that we will get that information. Whether this process is easy or hard is up to you, whether it takes one hour or one week is up to you. said Eshaq. Karim was shaking with fear. First things first, why dont you tell us about the objective of your mission? Unless I am mistaken, your vessel was captured near to Etherniasti, a few days before the missile attack, what were you doing there? Karim didnt speak. WHAT WERE YOU DOING! shouted Eshaq.
I- I- I dont know entirely, Im just a crewman, I dont make decisions. Replied Karim.
Well what do you know? Said Eshaq angrily.
I- I know that W- We were carrying out some kind of intelligence mission, S- S- Something about defence W- weaknesses, said Karim as he continued to tremble in his chair.
Is it possible that this was to find targets for this missile attack?
N- no, I- I- dont know. I think th- th- the missiles were in retaliation for our c- capture,
Good, good. Thank you for cooperating with us. There is one last question I would like to ask you, can you pinpoint the location of the High command. We have a map here, if you could simply point it out.
I- I- dont know, like I- I said, Im j- just a crewman, Ive never been to h- h- high command,
Well, thank you for again for being cooperative. Eshaq said, as a smile spread across his face. The guards unstrapped Karim and took him back to his cell, still shaking.
